## How it works

- [statement] Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov report approximately linear short-horizon price impact of order-flow imbalance with depth-dependent slope in their US equity sample. (low confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1011.6402 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion
- [statement] Huang-Lehalle-Rosenbaum model order-flow intensities as functions of current order-book state during periods of constant reference price. (low confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1312.0563 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion
- [statement] Both Huang-Lehalle-Rosenbaum and Albers et al. explicitly include queue state and order priority or position when analyzing passive execution outcomes. (medium confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1312.0563 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Chávez-Casillas-Figueroa-López show in their LOB description that touch depletion and, when the spread exceeds one tick, new orders inside the spread are distinct mechanisms for changes in best quotes. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1407.5684v3 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion
- [statement] Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov report a short-interval approximately linear association between order-flow imbalance and price changes, with impact slope inversely related to depth. (low confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1011.6402 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion
- [statement] Huang, Lehalle and Rosenbaum model order-flow intensities as functions of current book state within constant-reference-price intervals. (low confidence) — https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1312.0563 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Gould-Bonart and Albers et al. both define top-of-book imbalance as bid quantity minus ask quantity divided by their sum. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03492 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Gould-Bonart report out-of-sample next-midprice classification gains in their Nasdaq sample; Albers et al. describe more common imbalance-aligned next-price cases than reversal cases in their Binance sample. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03492 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] DeLise and Albers et al. both document adverse post-fill midprice drift for passive orders in their respective Treasury-futures simulation and Binance Bitcoin-perpetual experiment. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] In the Albers live Binance experiment, naive two-sided maker quoting and the examined simple imbalance strategies perform poorly despite spread capture and rebates. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion
- [statement] Albers et al. state that a favorable imbalance can leave a maker order at the end of the longer queue with low fill probability, whereas taking liquidity pays the taker fee. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion
- [statement] Chávez-Casillas-Figueroa-López identify constant one-tick spread, fixed order volume and queue reset after depletion as restrictive assumptions, and propose preserving the un-depleted opposite queue with variable spread. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1407.5684v3 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion
- [statement] Gould and Bonart report one-tick-ahead predictive information from bid/ask queue imbalance, with stronger classification improvement for large-tick stocks. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03492 · keywords: Order-book geometry and queue depletion
